23	// resolveCheckpointBackendType maps a user-facing backend name to the canonical
24	// settings backend type and validates it may serve as the primary. It accepts
25	// the friendly aliases "branch"/"refs" and the canonical "git-branch"/"git-refs"
26	// (case-insensitive). An unknown or non-git-backed value is rejected via the
27	// checkpoint registry, so the error text stays in sync with the backend list.
28	func resolveCheckpointBackendType(name string) (string, error) {
29		typ := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(name))
30		switch typ {
31		case checkpointBackendBranchAlias:
32			typ = checkpoint.BackendTypeGitBranch
33		case checkpointBackendRefsAlias:
34			typ = checkpoint.BackendTypeGitRefs
35		}

37			return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid --%s: %w", flagCheckpointBackend, err)
38		}
39		return typ, nil
40	}

42	// applyCheckpointBackend sets the primary checkpoint backend on settings,
43	// preserving any existing mirrors except one whose type would collide with the
44	// new primary (the one-of-each-type topology rule enforced in checkpoint.Open).
45	// Switching the primary on an existing repo is safe: new checkpoints use the new
46	// backend while read routing keeps prior checkpoints readable in their original
47	// format.
48	func applyCheckpointBackend(s *EntireSettings, typ string) {
49		cfg := s.Checkpoints
50		if cfg == nil {
51			cfg = &settings.CheckpointsConfig{}
52		}
53		cfg.Primary = settings.BackendConfig{Type: typ}
54		cfg.Mirrors = slices.DeleteFunc(cfg.Mirrors, func(m settings.BackendConfig) bool {

56		})

19	// eligibleImport pairs a just-selected agent with its importer and the number
20	// of sessions discoverable for the current repo within the lookback window.
21	type eligibleImport struct {
22		imp          agentimport.Importer
23		displayName  string
24		sessionCount int
25	}
26	
27	// Seams for testing the orchestration in maybeOfferSessionImport without disk
28	// discovery, a real TTY, or real checkpoint writes. Production wiring uses the
29	// real implementations below.
30	var (
31		sessionImportDiscover = discoverImportableAgents
32		sessionImportPrompt   = promptImportSelection
33		sessionImportRun      = runSelectedImports
34	)
35	
36	// maybeOfferSessionImport offers, on first-time enable only, to import
37	// pre-existing agent history for the just-selected agents. Granularity is
38	// agent-level: choosing an agent imports all its discoverable sessions (30-day
39	// lookback, matching `entire import`). It is best-effort — discovery or import
40	// failures are logged and reported to the user but never fail enable.
41	//
42	// Import only happens on an explicit choice: an interactive run presents a
43	// multi-select (nothing pre-checked) and imports what the user selects; `--yes`
44	// ("accept all defaults") auto-imports all eligible agents. A non-interactive
45	// run without `--yes` (a script, a piped shell, or an agent with no TTY) makes
46	// no choice, so it imports nothing and just points at `entire import` — silently
47	// importing history there would be surprising.
48	func maybeOfferSessionImport(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, agents []agent.Agent, opts EnableOptions, firstRun bool) {
49		if !firstRun {
50			return
51		}
52	
53		repoRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
54		if err != nil {
55			// No worktree root => nothing to import against. Enabling still succeeds.
56			logging.Warn(ctx, "session import offer skipped: no worktree root", "error", err)
57			return
58		}
59	
60		eligible := sessionImportDiscover(ctx, agents, repoRoot)
61		if len(eligible) == 0 {
62			return
63		}
64	
65		selected := eligible
66		if !opts.Yes {
67			if !interactive.CanPromptInteractively() {
68				// Non-interactive without --yes: don't silently import. Leave a
69				// pointer so scripted/agent enables can still import on demand.
70				logging.Info(ctx, "session import offer skipped: non-interactive without --yes", "eligible", len(eligible))
71				fmt.Fprintf(w, "Found importable history for %s. Run 'entire import <agent>' to import it.\n", pluralAgents(len(eligible)))
72				return
73			}
74			selected, err = sessionImportPrompt(ctx, w, eligible)
75			if err != nil {
76				// Best-effort: a prompt/UI failure must never fail enable. Log,
77				// note it, and skip import.
78				logging.Warn(ctx, "session import offer skipped: prompt failed", "error", err)
79				fmt.Fprintf(w, "Note: could not show import prompt: %v\n", err)
80				return
81			}
82		}
83		if len(selected) == 0 {

90	// discoverImportableAgents keeps the selected agents that have a registered
91	// importer and at least one discoverable session for the repo.
92	func discoverImportableAgents(ctx context.Context, agents []agent.Agent, repoRoot string) []eligibleImport {
93		now := time.Now()
94		var out []eligibleImport
95		for _, ag := range agents {
96			imp := importerForAgent(ag)
97			if imp == nil {
98				continue
99			}
100			sessions, err := imp.Discover(repoRoot, "", now, nil)
101			if err != nil {
102				logging.Warn(ctx, "session import discovery failed", "agent", string(ag.Type()), "error", err)
103				continue
104			}
105			if len(sessions) == 0 {
106				continue
107			}
108			out = append(out, eligibleImport{
109				imp:          imp,
110				displayName:  string(ag.Type()),
111				sessionCount: len(sessions),

Explanation confirmed — this is two bugs stacking, and the repo not having entire before is exactly what triggers it.

## What actually happened

`entire enable` on a **first run** does two things the user didn't see coming:

1. **First-run default backend is `git-refs`** — `firstRunCheckpointBackendDefault()` in `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go:1384` returns `"refs"`, so checkpoints are written as `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>`. (The config-less runtime fallback is still `git-branch`, which is why this only shows up on fresh enables.)

2. **First-run enable offers to import pre-existing agent history** — `maybeOfferSessionImport` (`setup.go:1324` → `setup_import.go:48`). Claude Code + Cursor were detected, so it discovered up to 30 days of local session transcripts and imported them as checkpoints. **That's where the refs come from**: they aren't pre-existing entire data, they're being *created right then* from the user's local Claude/Cursor session files. One ref per imported turn — hence dozens.

Then the user hit Ctrl-C mid-import:

- `cmd/entire/main.go:50` cancels the root context and prints "Interrupting… press Ctrl-C again to force quit" — but the process keeps running.
- `agentimport.Run` (`cmd/entire/cli/agentimport/agentimport.go:188`) has **no `ctx.Err()` check anywhere** in its session or turn loops, and the write path doesn't cancel either: `gitRefsStore.writeSession` (`checkpoint/refs_store.go:228`) has no ctx guard (unlike its `backfill*`/`List` siblings at 261/291/315/498), and `CreateCommit` (`checkpoint/persistent.go:2460`) ignores ctx entirely. So the import runs on to completion.
- The *only* ctx-aware step left in that path is `enqueueForPush` → `PushQueueForRepo` → `resolveGitCommonDir` (`checkpoint/git_common_dir.go:24`), which shells out `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` via `exec.CommandContext`. With a canceled ctx that fails instantly → **one WARN per imported turn**, at ~8/s. That's the flood.

And it's on the terminal rather than in `.entire/logs/entire.log` because **`entire enable` never calls `logging.Init`** (`import_cmd.go:64` does; the setup path doesn't). With no package logger, `logging.log` falls back to `slog.Default()` (`logging/logger.go:239`), which routes through the std `log` package — exactly the `2026/08/06 12:23:06 WARN msg key=value` format in the paste.

## Why it's not just cosmetic

Every checkpoint written after the Ctrl-C landed locally but was **never enqueued for push**. The push queue is the *sole* discovery mechanism — `pushqueue.go:20` says so explicitly ("the git-refs backend cannot push every local checkpoint ref at pre-push time... each write records the ref it touched here"). And import is idempotent by design: a re-run sees the checkpoint ID in `existing` and skips the turn entirely, so it never re-enqueues. Those checkpoints are permanently local-only and will never reach the dashboard.

`MigrateBranchToRefs` guards against precisely this — `migrate.go:120-132` re-enqueues already-imported refs with a comment about a prior run crashing between `setRef` and `Enqueue`. The import path has the hole that migration explicitly plugged.

Minor smell also worth noting: `enqueueForPush` resolves the git common dir on *every* write, so importing N turns spawns N `git rev-parse` subprocesses.

## Fix

1. `ctx.Err()` checks at the top of `agentimport.Run`'s session and turn loops (and a guard in `gitRefsStore.writeSession`, for parity with the backfill paths) so Ctrl-C actually stops the import.
2. Call `logging.Init` in the enable/setup path so its warnings go to `.entire/logs/` like every other command's.
3. Optionally memoize the git common dir per store so the push queue isn't re-resolved per write — that also makes the warning fire once instead of N times.

For the affected user, the orphaned refs can be recovered by appending `{"ref":"refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>"}` lines to `entire-checkpoint-push-queue.jsonl` in the git common dir; the next push flushes them.

| Path | Behavior |

So `--yes` ("accept all defaults") does the *opposite* of the interactive default. The doc comment at `setup_import.go:43` claims "Import only happens on an explicit choice" and counts `--yes` as one — but `--yes` is a statement about setup defaults, not consent to ingest 30 days of local agent transcripts into git refs (and, once logged in, push them). The non-interactive path returns early at ~1717 and never prints that line — so they were on either the interactive form or `--yes`. ## Does it show up in output?

In the terminal, yes — but nothing durable:
- During the run: a spinner, `Importing Claude Code sessions... (session 3/12 · turn 40/57)` — drawn with `\r\033[K` on a single line (`progress.go:87`), so it leaves no scrollback.
- On completion: `Imported N turn(s) from M session(s)` — persistent, but only reached after `agentimport.Run` returns.

That's also why the paste is visually mangled: the spinner goroutine has no ctx awareness either, so after Ctrl-C it keeps redrawing on stdout while the WARNs stream to stderr, and the two shred each other's lines.

No — and that's the sharper half of it. Because `entire enable` never calls `logging.Init`, **every** `logging.*` call under the import goes to `slog.Default()` → stderr:

- `session import discovery failed` (`setup_import.go:102`)
- `session import skipped: checkpoint policy not satisfied` (`:215`)

- `import: turn anchor fell back` (`agentimport.go:259`)

2. Print a durable line *before* the import starts (`Importing history from Claude Code, Cursor (2 agents, ~180 turns)...`), not just a transient spinner, so an interrupted run leaves a trace.

## Changes

**1. Enable now routes its logging to a file** — `setup.go:884`. `logging.SetLogLevelGetter` + `logging.Init` right after the git-repo check (so it can't create `.entire/logs/` outside a repo). Every `logging.*` call under setup previously fell through to `slog.Default()` → the user's terminal. Note the irony this fixes: `refs_store.go:551` comments that "logging.Warn alone lands only in `.entire/logs/`" — which was false for the entire enable flow.

**4a. Import stops on Ctrl-C** — `agentimport.go`, `ctx.Err()` checks at the top of the session loop and the turn loop.

**4b. The git-refs store rejects canceled writes** — `refs_store.go:228`. This was the actual root cause: the git-branch store guards its writes (`persistent.go:865` and 7 more), and the refs store's own `backfill*`/`List`/`GetCheckpointAuthor` all guard — but `writeSession`, the create path, didn't. Since first-run enable defaults to git-refs, the reported flow was the one configuration with no brake.

**4c. The push-queue record survives shutdown** — `enqueueForPush` now resolves the queue via `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`. By that point the ref is already on disk (go-git ref writes ignore ctx), and the queue is the sole push-discovery mechanism, so honoring cancellation there stranded checkpoints permanently — the writers are idempotent, so no later run re-enqueues them. This is also what fires the warning per turn, so the flood itself is gone.

**Plus** interrupted-import handling in both callers: `runSelectedImports` now breaks instead of proceeding to the *next* agent's history after a Ctrl-C, and both it and `entire import` report `Import interrupted after N turn(s)` with a resume hint rather than a raw `context canceled`.

fix(checkpoint): make git-refs writes respect cancellation, but never drop push bookkeeping

The git-refs store was the one write path with no brake on a canceled
context. The git-branch store guards its writes, and this store's own
backfill/read methods guard theirs, but writeSession — the create path —
did not. Nothing downstream of it observes ctx either (go-git object and
ref writes and CreateCommit all ignore it), so a bulk writer that itself
ignored cancellation kept minting checkpoints after Ctrl-C.

The one step that DID observe the canceled ctx was the push-queue
resolution, which shells out to `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` — so
every post-cancel write logged "resolve push queue failed; ref not
enqueued" and left its ref out of the queue. That is worse than noisy:
the queue is the only push-discovery mechanism there is, and the writers
are idempotent, so no later run re-enqueues a missed ref. Those
checkpoints were stranded locally forever.

Resolve the queue with the cancellation stripped instead. By that point
the ref is already on disk, so the bookkeeping that makes it pushable
has to complete too — it is a local, sub-millisecond step, and a second
Ctrl-C still force-quits the process.
